rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.proposedConceptualExplanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons. Combustion is a reaction with oxygen that produces carbon dioxide and water in the complete case, and releases energy. A symbolic balanced example for methane is CH4 + 2 O2 -> CO2 + 2 H2O. Substitution is a different reaction class, where a hydrogen on an alkane framework can be replaced by another atom or group. Combustion generates oxidation products, while substitution yields a substituted organic derivative. This is a theoretical distinction and does not describe performing any reaction.
proposedFiveMarkCriteria: Recognize alkanes as saturated hydrocarbons and identify two different reaction classes
Explain carbon dioxide and water as products of complete combustion
Give a correct balanced symbolic example for methane combustion
Describe substitution conceptually as replacement of an alkane hydrogen
Contrast combustion products with a substituted hydrocarbon derivative

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.proposedConceptualExplanation: An unsaturated hydrocarbon has a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, whereas an alkane contains only single carbon-carbon bonds. Adding hydrogen across an alkene double bond can produce a saturated hydrocarbon; the relationship can be represented by the balanced theoretical expression C2H4 + H2 -> C2H6. The broad name of the transformation is hydrogenation. Industrial chemical reactions of this family are commonly discussed in relation to catalysis, without the catalyst becoming a net product. The carbon skeleton is retained as unsaturation decreases. These are textbook concepts, not experimental directions.
proposedFiveMarkCriteria: Differentiate unsaturated multiple bonding from alkane single-bond structures
Identify the alkene-to-alkane hydrogen-addition reaction category
Write the theoretical balanced ethene-to-ethane relationship
Recognize the concept of catalysis without procedural details
Relate reduction in bond unsaturation to saturated product classification

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.proposedConceptualExplanation: A soluble salt dissolves appreciably in water, while an insoluble salt has low water solubility. A neutralization reaction between an acid and a suitable base can be discussed as one general conceptual source of dissolved salt and water. A soluble salt is associated with an aqueous phase, while the formation of an insoluble salt may be understood through precipitation of ions from solution. The separation principles differ: a dissolved substance is distinct from a precipitated solid. Choice of a salt classification must be justified by its actual solubility rather than its name. This is a comparison of chemical principles, not directions for carrying out laboratory preparations.
proposedFiveMarkCriteria: Distinguish soluble from insoluble salts by aqueous solubility
Recognize neutralization as a class of salt-forming reaction
Identify the meaning of a dissolved salt in an aqueous phase
Recognize precipitation as a class of insoluble-salt formation
Differentiate a precipitated solid from a dissolved product conceptually

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.proposedConceptualExplanation: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl (-COOH) functional group and show characteristic acid reactions. In a theoretical reaction with an appropriately reactive metal, an acid may form a salt while producing hydrogen gas. Acid-base neutralization yields a salt and water. Reactions with carbonates are recognized through the general products salt, water and carbon dioxide. Carboxylic acids are also discussed in organic chemistry as one reactant family involved in ester formation with alcohols. These are broad product classifications, not practical instructions for using chemicals.
proposedFiveMarkCriteria: Identify the carboxyl functional group and typical acid behavior
State conceptual salt and hydrogen formation with an appropriate metal
Identify salt and water as neutralization products
Identify salt, water and carbon dioxide as the carbonate reaction products
Recognize ester formation as a broad organic reaction category
